issues.claim: The base states the tail's order three ways and none matches the stages' home. II.7.6's code-block comment: "Tail stages registered after the network stage by declared I/O (§4.12): the systems in the order ruin, catacomb, cavern, quarry, vaults and … buried system …; then II.7.3's stage, the access pass, II.7.5's stage; then the connection stage last" — U-FRONT (II.7.3's stage) before the access pass. II.7.4's `UndergroundStrategy` comment declares its inputs as `under.tunnels`, the ground plat, the fields and the underground `Allocation` — no output of the access pass. §4.12's list names `UndergroundSystemStrategy`, `UndergroundStrategy`, `UndercityStrategy`, `UndergroundLinkStrategy` and no access pass (VPC-17 proposes inserting it after `UndergroundStrategy`, which would repeat the wrong order). V04 §3.1, the stages' home, orders T1 U-NET, T2 U-SYS, **T2b U-ACCESS, T3 U-FRONT** (T3 reads "the excavation reading (F6)" that T2b writes: F6's dwellings stand only in accessible cavern and ruin clusters, item 109 (j) (4)), T4 U-CITY, T5 U-LINK, T6, T8; V07 §3.16 (1) registers the same order at village rungs; II.7.6's prose ("after the void systems and before the undercity") agrees with V04. Run in the base comment's order, U-FRONT places F6's void dwellings before any excavation reading exists — a different generator.
issues.required_change: II.7.6's comment reads "…; then the access pass (`AccessPassStrategy`, U-ACCESS), II.7.3's stage (U-FRONT, which reads the access pass's excavation reading for F6), II.7.5's stage; then the connection stage last (V04 §3.1)". II.7.4's `UndergroundStrategy` comment adds to its inputs the access pass's outputs (its access points, links and `ExcavationRecord`; V04 §3.1 T3). §4.12's list reads "`SewerStrategy` (U-NET), then `UndergroundSystemStrategy`, `AccessPassStrategy`, `UndergroundStrategy`, `UndercityStrategy` and last `UndergroundLinkStrategy`, each `phase: 'tail'`, in V04 §3.1's order" (this supersedes VPC-17's proposed wording).

issues.claim: PART III's rung-rows paragraph: "`layers.sewers.existence = 'never'` (II.7.1: no network stage registers, a request's `toggles.sewers` reported as not applicable, the `drain` column read by nothing)"; II.7.1: "Without a network — a TOWN whose draw came out `off`, every village — the rule does nothing". V04 §3.1 *The maintenance mode* and J-V4.90 (every inherited system, "the sewer network and the undercity included", stays registered at a village rung, re-derived from its kept elements, never grown) and V07 §3.12 (a shrunk town's systems "stay registered in maintenance mode") say a network stage is registered at a village rung that inherited a network; PART III's own next paragraph says the same.
issues.required_change: PART III's parenthesis reads "(II.7.1: no network is laid at a village rung — the network stage registers there only in V04 §3.1's maintenance mode for a network a larger rung left —; a request's `toggles.sewers` reported as not applicable, the `drain` column read by nothing)"; II.7.1's "every village" reads "every village that holds no inherited network (V04 §3.1's maintenance mode)".

issues.claim: §4.5 *Which districts*: "S12c covers the ground's districts; a unit run (a sky island's, a standalone neighbourhood document's) runs its own S12c over its districts (V01 §3.10)". V01 §3.10.3 step 5 ("The town's S12c and S13a include the island's districts"), V05 §3.1 (SKY-F "after the pool's merge, before S12c — which gives the island's districts their character and identity as it gives the ground's") and V05 §1b ("S12c, which runs after SKY-F") put a sky island's districts in the town's one S12c, after SKY-F; CF-PIPE-06's ruling says the same. The verify-pipeline report marked S12c done; the text still disagrees.
issues.required_change: §4.5 *Which districts* reads "S12c covers the ground's districts and the districts of every sky island (the town's S12c, after SKY-F; V01 §3.10.3 step 5, V05 §3.1); a standalone neighbourhood document's unit run runs its own S12c over its districts (V01 §3.10). The hinterland, sky and underground pseudo-districts take no character …".

issues.claim: The undercity's void-source rank (item 109 (e): a ruin ranks above caverns and quarries) has two homes with two shapes: II.7.5's `UndercityRule.sourceRank: Partial<Record<UndergroundSystem['kind'], number>>` ("ruin above cavern and quarry (V11)") and II.7.5 (1)'s prose "ranked … by the rule's `sourceRank`", against V04 §2.3's `RuinRule.sourceWeight: Record<UndergroundSystem['kind'], number>` ("the undercity's rank: V11 §3.23.6's row"), which V04 P6 and U-CITY C1 read as `capacity × RuinRule.sourceWeight[kind]` and V11 §3.23.6 and V12's register carry. A rank and a weight are not one reading; nothing in V04, V11 or V12 reads `sourceRank`.
issues.required_change: II.7.5 drops `sourceRank` from `UndercityRule`; II.7.5 (1) reads "a ruin (… ranked above caverns and quarries by `RuinRule.sourceWeight`, V04 §2.3; V11 §3.23.6: a void's capacity × its kind's weight orders the sources)".

issues.claim: `forecastSafety` (0.85) and `accessForecastMin` are declared twice: II.7.4's `UndergroundRule` (`voidDwellingHouseholds: number; accessForecastMin: number; forecastSafety: number /* 0.85 */`), which the base's S7b (6)–(7) caps read (§4.5, II.7.3, II.7.5), and V04 §2.3's `UnderLayoutRule` (`tables/under/layout.json`: `forecastSafety /* 0.85 */`, `accessForecastMin /* 0.5 */`), which V04 §8 registers for calibration. Two editable cells for one constant can be edited apart.
issues.required_change: V04 §2.3's `UnderLayoutRule` drops `forecastSafety` and `accessForecastMin` and cites II.7.4's `UndergroundRule` (the base's S7b reads them); V04 §3.3 P7, V04 §1b.1 and V04 §8's register row cite that home; the default 0.5 for `accessForecastMin` is written once, at II.7.4.

issues.claim: `voidDwellingHouseholds` is a rule cell in the base and a derived count in V04. II.7.4 declares it a field of `UndergroundRule` (`voidDwellingHouseholds: number`, listed with `crowdingShare` as an `extension` cell zeroed by the parity presets); §4.5 S7b (6) (d) calls "its share an `extension` cell". V04 §2.4 (`NetworkForecast`) and §3.3 P7 compute it: Σ min(`voidDwellings.maxHouseholds`, capacity) over the counted cavern and ruin voids, capped at `voidDwellings.share` × the poorest band's households — its cells being V04 §2.3's `voidDwellings`. A builder reading II.7.4 stores an editable count; V04 derives it every run.
issues.required_change: II.7.4's `UndergroundRule` drops `voidDwellingHouseholds`; its comment reads "… as are `crowdingShare`, V04 §2.3's `voidDwellings.share` and the class table's …"; II.7.3 (d) and §4.5 S7b (6) (d) read "the void-dwelling part — V04 §3.3 P7's derived `voidDwellingHouseholds` (its cells V04 §2.3's `voidDwellings`) …".

issues.claim: II.7.4 *Limits*: "with every system's chance 0 (the parity presets) and `maxNeighbourhoods` 0 nothing of the layer runs but the caverns and ruins the site holds, which are drawn only under the view key `showUnexcavated`". With every chance 0 no cavern or ruin is laid (II.7.6's `UndergroundSystemRow`: "every chance 0 in the parity presets"); V04 §3.5 ("The parity presets set every chance to 0 …, the ruin toggle `off`") and T-V4-35 ("no ruin and no cavern at any rung (g item 109 (i)'s no-op pin)") hold none. Read literally, II.7.4 keeps caverns and ruins under the parity presets and breaks item 109 (i)'s no-op pin.
issues.required_change: II.7.4 *Limits* reads "… with every system's chance 0 and `maxNeighbourhoods` 0 (the parity presets) nothing of the layer runs — no cavern and no ruin at any rung (item 109 (i)'s no-op pin; V04 T-V4-35); outside the parity presets an unexcavated cavern or ruin draws only under the view key `showUnexcavated` (V04 §5.2; J-VI.19) …".

issues.claim: One name, two records. Model §2.6 declares `interface OpeningRow { dayType: string; openH: number; closeH: number }` (a building's opening hours; `Building.openingHours?: OpeningRow[]`, §10.2's `openingHours: OpeningRow[]`). V04 §2.3 declares `interface OpeningRow { kind: 'sinkhole'|'mouth'|'skylight'|'collapsed_shaft'|'ruin_entrance'; chance: number; coverM?: number }` (`tables/under/openings.json`), and the base's own II.7.6 signature `AccessPassStrategy.run(…, rules: { …; openings: OpeningRow[]; … })` means V04's — so the base's interfaces use one type name for two shapes. The matrix rated the subject `agree` (home "defined-in-several").
issues.required_change: V04 §2.3 renames its record `UnderOpeningRow` (table `tables/under/openings.json` unchanged), and every use follows: V04 §1.2, §1b.1, §2.3's table, §3.1 (T2b), §3.3 P7, §3.5.7 (e), §4.1; II.7.6's `AccessPassStrategy` signature (`openings: UnderOpeningRow[]`) and its comment; V07 §1b (W46) and §3.16 (3) (iii); V06 §3.18's readers (the access pass's tables, the public openings); V11's registry row (`under.openings`) and §3.23.7.

issues.claim: V04 §3.1 *At every rung* gives the tail at THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE as "T2 (ruin and cavern only — catacombs, quarries, vaults and the buried town keep TOWN and above — and the vaults step for the arch vaults and terminal cistern of a raised way …), T2b, T3's F6 only, T5 (L3, L5, L7), T6 and T8". V04 §3.5.1 (10) lays, below TOWN, a dossier catacomb record's charnel vault (one `ossuary` chamber of the `dug` system, `W_CATACOMB_BELOW_TOWN`) — a run of U-SYS's catacomb step at a village rung — and V07 §3.16 (1), registering "the village subset V04 §3.1 names", adds "T2's catacomb step run for a dossier catacomb fact alone, which lays V07 §2.4's charnel vault". The subset V07 points at omits the step V07 adds.
issues.required_change: V04 §3.1 *At every rung* reads "T2 (ruin and cavern — catacombs, quarries, vaults and the buried town keep TOWN and above —, the vaults step for the arch vaults and terminal cistern of a raised way, and the catacomb step for a dossier catacomb record alone, which lays its charnel vault (V04 §3.5.1 (10))), T2b, …".

issues.claim: V07 §3.16 (3) restates V04 §3.5.7's access rules with different rules. (i) Dig from above: V07 — "Every village building standing over a chamber or gallery within `DigRule.reachM` … of its footprint's floor … draws once, when it is built"; V04 §3.5.7 (d) — every building whose footprint overlaps an element whose top lies below its dig floor, or whose basement ring lies within `DigRule.planReachM` of one, with `depthFactor` 1 to `reachM`, decaying by `decayM` to 0 at `maxM`, and "the draw is compared at every derivation … one not yet made appears when the building's chance later rises above its draw". (iii) Public openings: V07 lists sinkhole, mouth, collapsed shaft, ruin entrance; V04 §3.5.7 (e) also lays a `skylight` (a `mouth` of role `light`) and bounds the collapsed shaft at cover ≤ 15 m. Read as written, V07 seals voids beyond `reachM` and never revisits a draw.
issues.required_change: V07 §3.16 (3) (i)–(iii) state the village's rows and readings only and cite the rules: "(i) Dug from above — V04 §3.5.7 (d)'s draw, at every village building, with the village classes' `DigRule.classRow` rows below"; "(ii) Wells — V04 §3.5.7 (f)"; "(iii) Public openings — V04 §3.5.7 (e)'s candidates and `OpeningRow` chances (a sinkhole under a field, the green or a common; a cave mouth; a skylight; a collapsed shaft under a field face or the green; a ruin entrance at its marker)"; the restated eligibility ("within `DigRule.reachM`") and timing ("when it is built") are dropped.

issues.claim: The measures of `dist.centre`, `dist.gate`, `dist.market` and `dist.harbour` at the rungs whose `frameLaw` is `territory` (file f item 576 (b)) are written in full twice: model §2.5 (*At the rungs whose `RungProfile.frameLaw` is `territory`* … the heart, the palisade's gates else the perimeter crossings, the principal market rank else the first nucleus's open space else the heart, the wharf's `quay` way else absent) and V07 §2.4's *profile and authored rows* paragraph (the same four measures restated). The base is the context vector's home (principle (1); the contract's home model §2.5).
issues.required_change: V07 §2.4 replaces the four measuring clauses by "At village rungs `nearCentre`, `nearGate`, `nearMarket` and `nearHarbour` read `dist.centre`, `.gate`, `.market` and `.harbour` as §2.5 measures them at territory rungs (item 576 (b))", keeping its own rule "a class row's 'at a port' reads 'a wharf is laid' — a row with no such form, finding no harbour, takes the base's closest option, reported (J-V7.111)".

issues.claim: Missed shared subject: the `raised` data key and its record. §4.1 publishes the key from the base's declaration layer at M3a (file f item 290 (4): BASE) — "the ground arena's parts from 1 … read as one data key … so a product's stage may declare it as an input" — and types it only by "V07 §2.7's `RaisedRead`"; §4.12's `DataKey` comment lists `'raised'`. The record is declared only in V07 §2.7, a volume built at V-M1, so the base's own key has no base declaration (MC-11's rule: every type a base mechanism uses is declared in the base; canon S3). Verdict: home inverted; the shapes also disagree (VAL-13).
issues.required_change: §4.1 (beside *The `raised` key*) declares `RaisedRead` as a derived view over `RaisedWayRecord` (§2.7) — the way, its kind, `origin` (derived), `reason?: RaisedReasonKey`, the deck strip, the supports with their keys and `state`, the two feet (once VK0-05/06's feet are in §2.2/§2.7), the spans `{ a; b; state }` with `'standing'` for an absent state, an aqueduct's channel — and V07 §2.7 cites it ("`RaisedRead` is §4.1's").

issues.claim: V07 §2.7's `RaisedRead` disagrees with `RaisedWayRecord` (§2.7), the record it reads: its spans are keyed `{ from; to; state }` where the base keys a span by `a`, `b` (the bounding piers' keys) and `DeclineOp`'s `SpanRef` by `from`/`to` support ordinals; its `supports: PolygonCm[]` drops each support's key and `state?: 'ruined'|'cleared'` (V06's decline, BCR-V6-26); its `reason?: string` is the base's `RaisedReasonKey`. V07 §3.5a (3)–(6) then treat every support as an obstacle (turning trackers), as a hole in fields and closes, and as a stretch the palisade abuts — so a pier V06 has `cleared` (taken down, stone credited) still blocks the village.
issues.required_change: V07 §2.7 (or §4.1 once VAL-12 lands) types `supports: { key: number; ring: PolygonCm; state?: 'ruined'|'cleared' }[]`, `spans: { a: number; b: number; state: 'standing'|'ruined'|'cleared' }[]` and `reason?: RaisedReasonKey`; V07 §3.5a (3), (4), (5) and (6) read "a support whose `state` is absent or `ruined`" (a `cleared` support is neither an obstacle nor a hole nor a stretch the palisade abuts).

issues.claim: V07 §3.9 (1) puts the village land budget in "the farm table's village rows (§4.9's `FarmTable` at the village rungs)": arable 1.2 ha per head, **meadow 0.15, pasture and commons 0.6**, fuel and timber by the base's law — summed into the territory's 2.275 ha per head (E-38: "derived as the sum of the FarmTable village rows"; V07 §2.2, V12's register). §4.9's `FarmTable { arableHaPerCapita, householdsPerFarmstead, fieldHaPerFarmstead, fuelM3PerCapitaYear, timberM3PerCapitaYear, coppiceM3PerHaYear, woodM3PerHaYear, extent, reserveArable }` has no meadow or pasture-and-commons column, so two of the five summed cells have no home and E-38's derived sum cannot be computed from the table.
issues.required_change: §4.9's `FarmTable` gains `meadowHaPerCapita` and `pastureHaPerCapita` (the pasture and commons per head; read at the territory rungs by V07 §3.2 (1)'s land law and §3.9 (1); at base rungs by §4.9's hinterland presets as they stand), the village rows' values staying as E-38 places them (V07 §3.9 (1): 0.15 and 0.6; V12's register holding the farm rows); V07 §3.9 (1) names the two cells.

issues.claim: Missed shared subject: `PlanForm`. §4.9's `FarmModeRow { …; form?: PlanForm /* read only at village rungs */; … }` uses a type declared only at V07 §2.2 (`type PlanForm = 'grown'|'street'|'green'|'nucleated'|'polyfocal'|'row'| 'dispersed'`), with no pointer; the matrix lists `FarmModeRow` but not `PlanForm`. Verdict: the values agree (V07 §3.2 (3) maps the forms to `perimeter` and `fill`), the base names no home.
issues.required_change: §4.9's `FarmModeRow` comment reads `form?: PlanForm /* V07 §2.2's plan forms; read only at village rungs (V07 §3.2 (3)) */` — or, under MC-11's rule, `PlanForm` is declared in §4.9 beside the row and V07 §2.2 cites it.

issues.claim: V07 §1 *Out of scope*: "Floating islands (none reaches a village rung: §4.11 fells an island when the CITY band is left, and TOWN holds none)". §4.11 (*Islands and the underground over epochs*: an island whose settlement falls below the CITY band "wanes, settles after its dwell band and falls"), II.6 (6), V05 §3.15 (6) ("A rung crossing downward makes every island's target 0: they wane, settle and fall over their dwells, never in one epoch") and V07's own §3.12 ("An island still waning or settled when the fold gives the village product continues V05's steps") say an island can stand over a village for its dwell spans.
issues.required_change: V07 §1 reads "Floating islands are V05's: no new island arises at a village rung (`layers.islands` `none`), and an island a fallen city leaves wanes, settles and falls over its dwells at whatever rung (V05 §3.15 (6); V07 §3.12), the village phases reading none".

issues.claim: V05 §5.1 *Sheets*: "every shipped sheet (`ink`, `lit`, `hatched`, `night` and the parity presets, which carry the rows though their recipes hold islands off) resolves every sky semantic, so the loader never refuses one". §8.2's presets table ships `parchment` and `bw-print` beside `night` as ink-family variants at M3b (RIC-01) and lists `painterly` (built by V07 at V-M1, a family at all four bands); none of the three is in V05's list, so their sheets are not required to carry `sky.island.*`, `sky.access.*`, `sky.fall`, `sky.mist` or the role `sky.ground`, and a sheet lacking a semantic is refused.
issues.required_change: V05 §5.1 reads "every shipped sheet — §8.2's presets table: `ink`, `lit`, `hatched`, the ink-family variants `parchment`, `bw-print` and `night`, `painterly` once V07 ships it, and the parity presets … — resolves every sky semantic"; the per-family table gives `parchment` and `bw-print` their `ink` rows and `painterly` its land, rim and access rows.

issues.claim: §9.1 declares `QuarterNode` "built by S6 (§4.5), named by S13a" (model §2.5: "§9.1's QuarterNode merge tree, built by S6 (§4.5)"; §4.5: "After typing, S6 builds §9.1's quarter merge tree … once"), and its *What the tree holds* lists the undercity leaves and the sewer's pseudo-district but no sky island. V05 §3.14 and V05 §1b make each island "the root of its own `QuarterNode` (members its districts, `cityCut` true), named with the island's name", produced by S13a after the unit run — districts S6 never sees. The island node's producer is named only in the volume, against the home's "built by S6".
issues.required_change: §9.1's comment reads "built by S6 (§4.5) — a sky island's root node by S13a over the island's districts after its unit run (V05 §3.14) —, named by S13a"; *What the tree holds* adds "each sky island is a root of its own, its members the island's districts, `cityCut` true (V05 §3.14)"; model §2.5's quarters comment follows.

issues.claim: §8.2's states table, chamber row ("its `Chamber.kind` … replace: `chamber` with the kind's fill — `ossuary` …, `workings` …, `cistern` in `water`, `streetVault` and `bridgeVault` the `vault` hatch, `storey` and `square` …, `cellar` and `storage` as `dug`, the ruin's kinds by `ruinMasonry` …") omits `archVault` and `market`. V04 §5.2 *Chamber fill by kind* states "§8.2's chamber row is keyed by `Chamber.kind`: `streetVault`, `bridgeVault` and `archVault` with the `vault` hatch (an arch vault in the shallowest band, its floor at grade; its door a daylight opening) … `market` as the undercity's plaza". By §8.2 an arch vault draws as a plain `chamber` floor; by V04 with the vault hatch.
issues.required_change: §8.2's chamber row adds "`archVault` the `vault` hatch (its floor at grade, its door a daylight opening; V04 §5.2) and `market` as the undercity's plaza (the ring walkway and stalls, V04 §5.2)".

issues.claim: §2.5 types `ContextVector.dist.wall: M` (always a distance; `harbour?: M` is the one optional member). V05 §3.11 writes, on an island, "`dist.wall` to an author's island wall (V05 §3.21), else none"; an unwalled TOWN and a village with no palisade have no wall either, and §2.5 states no value for them. A reader of V11's `wall` and `wallInner` rows (V11 §3.3.3) gets a number by §2.5's type and no target by V05.
issues.required_change: §2.5 types `wall?: M` "absent where the settlement (or a sky island) has no enceinte; a `wall` or `wallInner` row then finds no target, as a `harbour` row does where no harbour exists"; V05 §3.11's "else none" reads "else absent (§2.5)".

issues.claim: Hand-off XV-V9-8 is closed at its destinations differently from what V09 states. V09 §8: AP6 and AP7 "are priced with their own staged milestones — V04's M6-U, V05's P4 … outside the base total, as those engines are (V04 §8, V05 §8, V10 §8 and V02 §8 carry them)".
